title: PrimeCare B01–B18 deep assessment and repair plan
scope: Shared theme/skeleton B01–B18 and its actual app/service/release integration; not a claim that the whole PrimeCare platform was re-audited.
activity: Assessment and planning only; no application code, production permissions, provider operations or runtime activation changed in this assessment.
verdict: Shared foundations and tested subsets exist; full functional integration and production acceptance are not established for any whole batch.
evidenceLimits: Production metadata findings use the retained read-only CI snapshot 41346724602, not a new live database read during this assessment. Refresh before any write.
The 187 endpoint candidates are historical keyword candidates, not approved equivalent contracts or proof of runtime behavior.
Static constructor scanning does not resolve all dynamic factories; the repair plan requires a complete runtime composition inventory.
Local database integration uses PGlite; native PostgreSQL and desktop Flutter evidence comes from CI.
No authenticated production business journey, physical-device session or human review was performed in this assessment.
No completion percentage or reliable delivery duration is estimated from grouped gaps, file counts or component tests.

findings.title: Production grant identities do not reconcile
findings.detail: The production metadata snapshot contains 192 distinct grants: 64 each for API710, API857 and API777. Of those, 128 have labels for operations different from the message endpoints; all 192 refer to missing runtime artifact 1. These are overlapping findings, not 320 separate grant rows. API777 already has its correct preference key. Registry IDs 710/857 refer to endpoint IDs 4957/5104, which were absent from the endpoint readback. Numeric registry IDs must not be treated as endpoint IDs.
findings.repair: R01: reconcile original authority and exact row provenance; prepare a per-row before/after proposal. Do not blindly relabel, move grants, clear artifact references, invent artifacts, add roles or change quarantine.

findings.title: Source acceptance and publication have diverged
findings.detail: Tenant/PSW acceptance succeeded at 4c238052. Its publication job failed because main advanced to 83acb26c. The source comparison shows only two documentation files changed, but the publication guard compares the entire commit. This is a correctly enforced stale-source guard, with a scheduling/coordination consequence. Repeated documentation pushes can leave accepted code unpublished. The separate production grant blocker remains independently open.
findings.repair: R03: select the exact latest release candidate, finish required verification, publish that same immutable candidate, then record acceptance. Queue/retry stale candidates through a fresh verified run; retain both current-main checks.

findings.title: Shared implementation is much broader than actual host adoption
findings.detail: Static constructor scanning found one web composition of PrimeWorkModule/TenantTaskModulePort, in the existing tenant pilot, and no direct constructors of the assessed new workspace/navigation/work/communication/application adapters under the native apps or shared registry. This is bounded source evidence, not proof that no dynamic composition exists. The native usage guide explicitly states that existing shells do not opt in automatically. Tests and exports therefore cannot establish app-wide adoption.
findings.repair: R04/R05: build a per-app route-to-composition-to-adapter manifest, including dynamic registry resolution; bind registered hosts and verify actual routes before migration.

findings.title: Preference service is deliberately gated and does not cover the pilot roles
findings.detail: The handler requires PREFERENCE_SYNC_ENABLED=1, exact reviewed endpoint metadata, an active role and its API777 grant. The retained documentation says runtime is disabled, grants cover role IDs 1–64, Tenant Admin and Code Admin remain denied, and no registered panel bindings exist. Thus registering theme controls on Tenant Admin does not make account cloud preferences functional. Current secret/runtime flag values were not freshly queried during this assessment.
findings.repair: R02/R06: resolve actual raw-role/host authority, register panel references and intended preference kinds, wire explicit recovery, and enable only after exact authorization and deployed acceptance.

findings.title: The five work views implement task-backed subsets
findings.detail: Contacts is a read-only projection of users/clients. Notes edits task notes. Calendar changes task due dates. Board follows task transitions. This is useful reuse, but does not implement standalone contact/notes CRUD, timed appointments, recurrence, reminders, custom board lanes/ranking or new-template creation receipts. The broader platform may have related services; no platform-wide absence is claimed.
findings.repair: R08: reuse confirmed existing workflow contracts where equivalent; implement the missing domain flows only after request/response, authorization, persistence and receipt mapping.

findings.title: Communication templates omit full workflows
findings.detail: The collection adapter exposes existing message inbox/read/send/mark-read and owned mailbox reads. Its type explicitly excludes notifications; files project attachment references. These new templates do not yet supply general file storage management, mailbox compose/drafts/folders/delivery UI, full conversation creation/history/realtime/presence/call UI or a self-notification binding. Existing communications channels and provider services must be reused, not duplicated.
findings.repair: R09: map registered service operations to the inherited shared adapters; implement provider receipts, storage policies and real host flows with owned/cross-tenant denial.

findings.title: Several application/dashboard families are intentionally unavailable
findings.detail: Profile is read-only identity and settings manages shortcut preferences. Academy, commerce, AI images and help require additional confirmed workflows/providers. Dashboard projection supports project/analytics counts but explicitly returns unavailable for finance/crypto; invoice/pricing/authentication supporting-page statuses are also unavailable. These are missing integrations/features, not rendering regressions.
findings.repair: R10: confirm learning/help/finance/commerce/provider contracts and entitlements, reuse existing account flows, and complete genuine business flows without invented metrics or fixture success.

findings.title: Advanced controls and widget persistence are incomplete
findings.detail: Remaining B10 scope includes character-range rich-text marks/HTML import policy, spreadsheet/server query adapters, specialized rating/slider/stepper/transfer controls and production binary storage/picker adapters. The chart model accepts line, area, bar and donut, with metrics; free-coordinate grid editing and additional chart families remain outside the implemented subset. B11 has no registered dashboard preference document kind or complete authoritative widget mappings.
findings.repair: R07: specify each remaining variant, add shared web/native implementations and authorized persistence, and test real data/removal/readback. R06 must establish the dashboard document policy first.

findings.title: Durable restart recovery remains distinct from in-session retry
findings.detail: WorkModuleSession keeps the pending command, request key and acknowledgement in memory. The verified retry path avoids duplicate mutations after a failed readback. Disposing/restarting still clears this context; a durable restart journal/reconciliation flow is not implemented by that repair. Pending state must remain bound to tenant/user/raw role/dataset and receipt lifetime.
findings.repair: R06: add a scoped versioned pending-command journal and explicit restart reconciliation; test crash after send, lost acknowledgement, acknowledged/readback failure, receipt expiry, logout, revoked access and storage failure.

findings.title: Localization and terminology do not match complete rollout
findings.detail: The actual tenant work host hardcodes locale en. Generic pagination controls reuse Previous month/Next month translations even for non-calendar views. EN/FR/ES metadata exists, but translation presence is not reviewed business localization or whole-app RTL/accessibility acceptance.
findings.repair: R04/R11: propagate authenticated locale, register contextual pagination labels, and verify direction, date/number formats, keyboard/focus and screen-reader flows in real hosts.

findings.title: Reference parity and original-asset migration remain unclosed
findings.detail: The bounded proposal tracks 72 features, 24 core families and 389 reference files; it is not exhaustive parity certification. The reference audit retains 106 unadopted framework examples. The freshly reproduced asset inventory reports 105 original icons, 16 other original assets, 25 mapped shared-shell keys and 2,539 source files still using framework glyph tokens. That last count is an inventory, not 2,539 broken screens or a legal conclusion.
findings.repair: R11: assign every required reference a verified equivalent or explicit reviewed disposition, migrate app consumers progressively, and remove duplicates only after compatibility checks.

findings.title: Status/evidence records have drift and release checks are declarative
findings.detail: The older main audit still lists already-repaired B10 pinning/link-adapter work and a missing B17 catalogue. Newer evidence and source show those subsets exist. The draft evidence still says Flutter pending, although this assessment confirms the combined seven-job run passed on all three desktop OSes. check-theme-release.py validates declared booleans/presence of receipts, not their freshness or independent truth. All 18 batches still fail its release criteria; the 86 remaining-scope entries are grouped statements, not 86 unique bugs.
findings.repair: R00: reconcile one current evidence ledger with source/deployment/role/device scope and superseded links. Retain original historical receipts. Do not repair solved work again or promote batches from a green component suite.

findings.title: Production and physical-device acceptance is not established
findings.detail: Fresh local model/integration tests and historical/current CI cover important subsets, including test PostgreSQL and desktop Flutter. This assessment did not perform an authenticated production login/action/API/database/reload journey, live business mutation, physical Android/iOS test, screen-reader session or human release review. Passing desktop widget tests is not evidence for those gates.
findings.repair: R12: close feature/contract/host gaps, then run the full supported-app, role, tenant, locale and device acceptance matrix against the exact deployed source.

Create one per-item evidence ledger with exact source, API, metadata snapshot, deployment ID, actor/tenant, test and review scope.

tasks: Refresh SELECT-only endpoint, registry, permission, role and runtime-artifact rows from the pinned production authority; reconcile against original approved contracts, not numeric-ID similarity.
Produce the exact 192-row before/after proposal, including the 128 permission-key conflicts; explain whether each artifact reference should be restored, replaced or removed using its provenance.

Resolve genuinely missing business authority decisions only after source and governance evidence have been exhausted. Apply a narrowly scoped transaction with snapshot/drift guards, rollback and independent readback.
acceptance: No unintended new role, tenant, operation or artifact authority; existing denials and legitimate grants are preserved.
Unchanged identity guard passes without quarantine replacement or bypass; independent readback matches the approved row-level proposal.

repairPackages.title: Map existing service contracts before building replacements
tasks: Triage all 187 keyword candidates from 1,312 endpoint rows, beginning with scheduling, messaging/files, learning and finance. A keyword hit is not a contract.
For each requested action, resolve its existing implementation, canonical method/path, request/response, actor/tenant ownership, grants, tables, idempotency, receipts and provider entitlements.
Classify actions as reusable, implementation missing, contract missing or true product decision; specify only missing contracts and preserve existing API behavior.
acceptance: A requirement-to-contract matrix covers every business action with real source and authority evidence or an explicit blocker.
No fabricated API, screen, workflow, provider entitlement or business data.

repairPackages.title: Make verified publication reliable

acceptance: One candidate can progress from verification to publication without source drift; both current-main checks remain effective.
Deployment receipts and a smoke login/action/reload journey refer to the same source; rollback restores a compatible known-good API/UI pair.
